speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. I see you're experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to understand the severity and cause, let's start with your age and how long these symptoms have been present. Do you also notice any slurred speech, drooping eyelids, or changes in swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis

The pattern of worsening weakness with activity and improvement with rest, combined with double vision that fluctuates with gaze direction, strongly suggests Myasthenia Gravis. I will need to confirm this with specific antibody testing. REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR Antibodies, Anti-MuSK Antibodies, and Repetitive Nerve Conduction Study.
